Rashi on Arakhin 16b:10:1.english: How far - [Is] a person obligated to rebuke his fellow?

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:10:2.english: Until striking - Until this one becomes enraged and strikes the rebuker.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:10:3.english:
Until cursing - That he curses the rebuker.
Jonathan rebuked Saul until Saul became enraged.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:14:1.english: That he strikes - The host [strikes] the guest or his wife.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:14:2.english: Until he slings - The host [slings] the guest's belongings behind him, to throw them out of the house.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:15:1.hebrew: בהפשלה ובהכאה דאכסנאי גופיה, כ"ע לא פליגי — דתו לא מצי קאי. שמואל סבר: כיון דלדידיה אינו מכה, מאי נפקא ליה מיניה? הלכך, עד הפשלה:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:15:1.english: In [the case of] slinging [his belongings] and in [the case of] striking the guest himself, everyone agrees [that he may leave] — for he can no longer remain [there]. Shmuel holds: Since [the host] does not strike him [the guest], what difference does it make to him? Therefore, [he must remain] until [the host] slings [his belongings behind him].

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:16:1.english: And why all this - [Why is it necessary] for him to endure?

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:16:2.english: A guest - One who changes from his lodging.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:16:4.hebrew: ונפגם - הוא עצמו, דאמרי אינשי: כמה קשים אלו, שלא יוכלו לדור יחד:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:16:4.english: And is impaired - He himself [is impaired], for people say: "How difficult are these [people], that they could not live together!"

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:18:1.hebrew: למסעיו - בדרך שהיה רגיל לחנות ממסע למסע, שלא שינה בית מלוניו:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:18:1.english: On his journeys - Along the route that he was accustomed to encamp from journey to journey, [in] that he did not change his lodgings.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:18:2.hebrew: דאקראי - כגון אכסנאי שבדרך, שלן שם במקרה בעלמא, ששקעה לו שם חמה. למאן דאמר מאהלו, לא חשיב אלא אכסניא קבועה; ומאן דאמר ממסעיו, חשיב אפילו דאקראי:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:18:2.english: Temporary - Such as a traveler on the road who lodged there merely by chance, because the sun set upon him there. According to the one who says [it is derived] from "his tent," he considers only a permanent lodging; and the one who says [it is derived] from "his journeys" considers even a temporary [one].

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:1:1.english: In public - For it is for an act of sound that the robe atones.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:21:1.hebrew: תכלית יסורין - סוף מדת יסורין, כלומר: יסורין שאין פחותין מהן:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:21:1.english: The limit of suffering - The end of the measure of suffering — that is to say, suffering less than which there is none.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:21:2.hebrew: ואינו מתקבל עליו - שאינו למדתו כהגון, וצער הוא לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:21:2.english: And it does not suit him - That it is not to his size properly, and it causes him distress.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:21:3.english: To dilute - A cup of wine with hot water.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:22:1.hebrew: נהפך לו חלוקו - שלא לבשה כסדר, וצריך להופכה ולפושטה:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:22:1.english: His shirt turned inside out on him - That he did not put it on properly, and he needs to turn it and take it off.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:23:1.english: Three, and two came up in his hand - There is exertion to go back and take a third [coin].

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:24:1.hebrew: וכל כך למה - כלומר, למאי הילכתא הוו יסורין:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:24:1.english: And why all this - That is to say: For what halakha are [these considered] afflictions?

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:24:2.hebrew: קיבל עולמו - כל מנוחתו לעתיד. ואי עבר עליה חד מהנך, הרי הוא יסורין:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:24:2.english: He has received his world - All of his tranquility [destined] for the future. And if one of these [mishaps] befell him, behold, it is [considered] suffering.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:2:1.english: He separated - For on account of evil speech, plagues came upon him.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:3:1.hebrew: פטיט - לשון קול היוצא בחשאי, ובלע"ז פולי"ר:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:3:1.english: Chatter - An expression for a sound that comes out in secret, and in Old French, faveler [to chatter].

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:3:2.english: He shall bring a chattering offering - For the birds chirp constantly.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:4:1.english: One might [think that] he may not strike him - In a matter of rebuke.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:4:2.english: He slaps him - With the back of the hand.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:5:1.english: And his face changes - That he rebukes him in public, to whiten his face.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:6:1.hebrew: קיסם - כלומר, עון קטן שבידך. זה יכול לומר לו: "טול אתה עון גדול שבידך". הלכך, אין יכולין להוכיח, שכולן חוטאים:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:6:1.english: A splinter - That is to say, a minor sin that is in your hand. This [one] can say to him: "You remove the major sin that is in your hand." Therefore, they cannot rebuke, for they are all sinners.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:6:2.hebrew: שיודע להוכיח - דרך כבוד, שלא יהו פניו משתנין:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:6:2.english: [One] who knows [how] to rebuke - In a respectful manner, so that his face does not change [color].

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:7:1.english: [I would] complain about him - When I would see in him something unseemly.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:8:1.english: Rebuke for its own sake - For the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:8:2.hebrew: וענוה שלא לשמה - שעושה עצמו עניו, שאינו רוצה להוכיחו, ואותה ענוה שלא לשם שמים הוא, אלא שלא ישנאנו:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:8:2.english: And humility not for its own sake - That he makes himself [appear] humble, [in] that he does not want to rebuke him; and that humility is not for the sake of Heaven, but rather so that [the other] will not hate him.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:8:3.hebrew: דאמר מר - במסכת עבודה זרה בפ"ק (דף כ:): "ענוה גדולה מכולן", דכתיב: "יען משח אותי לבשר ענוים" — "לבשר חסידים" לא נאמר:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:8:3.english: As the Master said - In Tractate Avodah Zarah, in the first chapter (20b): "Humility is the greatest of all," as it is written: "Because [the Lord] has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble" — "to bring good tidings to the pious" is not stated.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:9:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבי חייא - לשמואל. "חזי מר דקא מצער לן רב הונא" — שמכה וחובט אותי:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:9:1.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him - To Shmuel. "See, Master, that Rav Huna is causing us distress" — that he strikes and beats me.

Rashi on Arakhin 16b:9:2.hebrew: כי נפק - חייא בר רב, אמר ליה רב הונא לשמואל: להכי מצערנא ליה, דהכי והכי עביד — דברים מגונים. והיינו ענוה שלא לשמה, דלא אמר ליה בפניו, ושלא בפניו סיפר בגנותו:
Rashi on Arakhin 16b:9:2.english: When he left - [When] Ḥiyya bar Rav [left], Rav Huna said to Shmuel: "For this [reason] I caused him distress, for he did such-and-such" — shameful things. And this is [what is meant by] humility not for its own sake: for he did not say [it] to him to his face, and [yet] not in his presence he spoke of his disgrace.

Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:13:1.hebrew: ומאן דאמר עד נזיפה הא כתיב הכאה וקללה - ואם תאמר: למאן דאמר נמי קללה, הא כתיב הכאה? וי"ל: שמא כדמשני, אגב חביבותא דיונתן. אי נמי: לא דריש ליה קרא ד"ויטל שאול", כיון דליתיה בהאי קרא ד"ויחר אף שאול", אלא קרא אחרינא הוא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:13:1.english: "And according to the one who says until reprimand, aren't hitting and cursing written?" - And if you say: According to the one who says [until] curse as well, isn't hitting written? And one can say: Perhaps [it is] as [the Gemara] answers: due to Jonathan's fondness [for David]. Alternatively, he does not expound the verse of "And Saul cast [the spear]," since it is not in this verse of "Then Saul's anger was kindled," but rather it is a different verse.

Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:19:1.hebrew: (לעיל) לעולם אל ישנה אדם מאומנות אביו ומאומנות אבותיו - ומייתי ראיה שאמו היתה מבני דן, ולקח לו אומנות אבותיו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:19:1.english: ([Referring to] above) "A person should never change from the craft of his father and from the craft of his ancestors" - And [the Gemara] brings proof that his mother was from the children of Dan, and he took for himself the craft of his ancestors.

Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:19:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "דאמר מר: אימיה מדן ואבוה מנפתלי" — דבדברי הימים (ב ב) כתיב: "ואמו מבני דן":
Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:19:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: "For the Master said: His mother was from Dan and his father was from Naphtali" — for in Chronicles (II Chronicles 2:13) it is written: "And his mother was from the children of Dan."

Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:8:1.hebrew: וענוה שלא לשמה - שעושה עצמו עניו ואינו רוצה להוכיחו, ואותה ענוה לא לשם שמים היא, אלא שלא ישנאנו. וי"מ: ענוה שלא לשמה — פירוש: משום גאוה, או שיאמרו: "אדם עניו הוא", ומשפיל עצמו ושותק בחירופו ועלבונו, ולא לשם שמים, אלא לקנות שם. אבל בקונט' שפירש ענוה שלא לשמה, שמונע תוכחה מן הצריכים — לא ישר אלי, דהוה רשע גמור:
Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:8:1.english: "And humility not for its own sake" - [This refers to one] who acts humble and does not want to rebuke [his fellow], and that humility is not for the sake of Heaven, but rather so that [his fellow] will not hate him. And some explain: "Humility not for its own sake" means [acting humbly] out of pride, or so that [people] will say: "He is a humble person," and he lowers himself and remains silent at his insult and humiliation, yet not for the sake of Heaven, but rather to acquire a reputation. However, that which was explained in the Kuntres — that "humility not for its own sake" [means] that he withholds rebuke from those who need it — does not seem right to me, for [in that case] he would be completely wicked.

Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:9:1.hebrew: חס ליה דליכסוף זרעיה דרב על ידאי - וזהו ענוה שלא לשמה, שהניחו לביישו משום כבוד אביו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 16b:9:1.english: "Heaven forbid that the offspring of Rav should be humiliated on my account" - And this is [the] humility not for its own sake — that he [Rav Huna] allowed him [Ḥiyya] to humiliate him, on account of the honor of his father [Rav].
